title: migrateLegacyWaitlist no longer replays legacy events on rebuild
detail: The legacy event stream of each migrated row is archived, so a projection rebuild does not resurrect the old id next to the imported entry. The report gains archivedStreams.

title: Waitlist gets linkOnSignup, a configurable submit rate limit, export and purge handlers and a status provisioned
detail: createWaitlistFeature({ linkOnSignup: true }) marks an invited entry provisioned, with linkedTenantId and provisionedAt, when its email becomes the first TenantAdmin member of a tenant; a multi-stream consumer on the membership event does this asynchronously. rateLimit replaces the default of 5 submits per IP per 10 minutes, or { disabled: true, reason } turns it off. waitlist:write:export and waitlist:write:purge are SystemAdmin-only (exportPurge: false leaves them out); purge needs confirmCount to match the current number of entries and shreds the personal-data keys only after every entry was forgotten. The entity gains the status provisioned and the column provisionedAt, so apps that mount the feature generate a schema migration. kumiko ops waitlist-migrate --from offlot|publicstatus [--dry-run] copies a legacy waitlist table into the entity idempotently. Details in docs/guides/waitlist.md.
migration: Apps that mount the waitlist feature run `kumiko schema generate <name>` and commit the migration: read_waitlist_entries gains the nullable column provisioned_at, and the status value provisioned is added. An app with its own waitlist (offlot-app, publicstatus, solon) mounts createWaitlistFeature() and copies the old rows with `kumiko ops waitlist-migrate --from offlot|publicstatus --dry-run` first. offlot-app keeps its legacy rows in the table read_waitlist_entries, the name the framework projection uses: copy or rename that table before the first boot and pass --source-table. The submit limit is keyed per IP and handler; behind a reverse proxy set trustedProxyHops, otherwise all visitors share one bucket of 5 submits per 10 minutes. With linkOnSignup the new consumer starts at the beginning of the event log and also provisions entries invited earlier.

title: Waitlist mails carry designer labels
detail: Feature and notify labels for confirmation and admin-notice name the waitlist mails in the document designer.

title: Waitlist invite no longer double-invites, uses the entry locale and refuses members
detail: Two parallel invite calls for one entry now queue on a per-entry advisory lock, so exactly one tenant and one invitation are created. The invitation mail is rendered in the entry's locale instead of the caller's. Inviting an email that already is a member of the target tenant fails with 422 waitlist_not_invitable, as reject already did.

title: Waitlist submit honors emailRateLimits: [], resolves notifyRecipient before the advisory lock and checks only open entries
detail: createWaitlistFeature({ emailRateLimits: [] }) no longer fails boot validation; the per-email bucket is dropped as documented. notifyRecipient runs before the per-email advisory lock and the entry insert, so a failing resolver can no longer abort the submit transaction or hold the lock; a throwing resolver only skips the admin notice. The duplicate check queries status pending or invited with limit 1 instead of scanning the first 50 rows of the address. The feature description now states that the response body is identical for known and unknown addresses while response timing can differ.

title: Waitlist confirmation and admin notice use template variables
detail: The confirmation and admin-notice mails are r.notification declarations (waitlist:notify:confirmation, waitlist:notify:admin-notice) with variables and localized templates. The notify data is the variable object; the confirmation wording is computed in code and passed as variables. The admin notice subject is the submitter name.
migration: Update delivery preferences and tests that referenced the old types or read the sections data. An app that mounts it without includeBundled needs template-resolver, renderer-foundation and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-mail-html at boot (composeRendererStack() from dev-server mounts all of them), plus a delivery with the channel-email feature; apps without the template tables need a schema migration (`kumiko schema generate`).

title: Waitlist notifyRecipient may return a promise
detail: Waitlist `notifyRecipient` may return a promise, so apps can read the admin address from config

title: Waitlist submit is limited per email address
Add waitlist bundled feature: public signup intake with admin invite and reject, GDPR export and erasure
Waitlist re-invite and reject no longer touch an invitee who already accepted
